ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is the input voltage source port Vin(t), marked with positive and negative terminals; the upper input terminal first has a 1 Ω resistor connected in series. The node at the right end of the resistor divides into two branches to the lower common loop: the middle branch is a 1 H inductor, and the right branch is a 2 H inductor. The arrow I is marked on the upper wire, pointing to the right-side 2 H inductor branch, indicating that what is required is the current flowing into the 2 H branch. Reasoning: Vin(t) is 0 when t<0, and steps to 15 V when t≥0. The two inductors are in parallel, so the equivalent inductance is L_eq = (1×2)/(1+2) = 2/3 H. This equivalent inductor is in series with the 1 Ω resistor, so the total current response is i_total(t) = (15/1)(1 - e^{-t/(L_eq/R)}) = 15(1 - e^{-1.5t}) A. The voltages across the parallel inductors are the same and the initial currents are 0, so the currents are distributed inversely proportional to the inductance values; the 2 H branch current is 1/3 of the total current. Therefore I(t) = 5(1 - e^{-1.5t}). Let I=2 A, obtaining 2 = 5(1 - e^{-1.5t}), so e^{-1.5t}=0.6, t = -ln(0.6)/1.5 ≈ 0.3405 s.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit from the image: after the 1 Ω resistor, the 1 H and 2 H inductors are in parallel, with the labeled current I flowing into the 2 H branch. From the text, take V_IN as a 0-to-15 V step at t=0 and the target I=2 A. Replace the two inductors by L_eq=(1×2)/(1+2)=2/3 H. The series RL current is i_total=15(1-e^{-t/(L_eq/R)})=15(1-e^{-1.5t}). Since the 2 H branch carries one-third of total current, I=5(1-e^{-1.5t}). Solve 2=5(1-e^{-1.5t}) to get t≈0.34 s.
